content: 1. Keusch GT discussed shigellosis in the book Bacterial Infections of Humans, edited by Brachman PS and Abrutyn E, published by Plenum Press in New York in 2009. 2. Raqib R and colleagues studied the persistence of local cytokine production during the acute and convalescent stages of shigellosis, with their findings published in Infection and Immunity in 1995 (Volume 63, Issue 1, Pages 289-296). 3. Keusch GT and Scrimshaw NS explored strategies for controlling diseases in developing countries, focusing on reducing the prevalence of infantile and childhood malnutrition through infection control. Their work appeared in Reviews of Infectious Diseases in 1986 (Volume 8, Issue 2, Pages 273-287). 4. Bejon P and colleagues analyzed the proportion of hospital admissions and deaths attributable to malnutrition among children in rural Kenya, with their findings published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2008 (Volume 88, Issue 6, Pages 1626-1631). 5. Scrimshaw NS, Taylor CE, and Gordon JE examined the interactions between nutrition and infection, publishing their findings in the American Journal of the Medical Sciences in 1959 (Volume 237, Issue 3, Pages 367-403). 6. Boschi-Pinto CL, Velebit, and Shibuya K estimated child mortality due to diarrhea in developing countries, with their research published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2008 (Volume 86, Issue 9, Pages 710-717). 7. Petri WA and colleagues reviewed the impact of enteric infections and diarrhea on human function and development, publishing their findings in the Journal of Clinical Investigation in 2008 (Volume 118, Issue 4, Pages 1277-1290). 8. Kotloff KL and colleagues assessed the global burden of Shigella infections and its implications for vaccine development and control strategies, with their work published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 1999 (Volume 77, Issue 8, Pages 651-666). 9. Snyder JD and Merson MH reviewed the global magnitude of acute diarrheal diseases using active surveillance data, with their findings published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 1982 (Volume 60, Issue 4, Pages 605-613). 10. Bern C and colleagues provided a ten-year update on the global burden of diarrheal diseases, publishing their findings in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 1992 (Volume 70, Issue 6, Pages 705-714). 11. Kosek M, Bern C, and Guerrant RL estimated the global burden of diarrheal diseases based on studies published between 1992 and 2000, with their work appearing in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2003 (Volume 81, Issue 3, Pages 197-204). 12. Parashar UD, Bresee JS, and Glass RI reviewed the global burden of diarrheal diseases in children, with their findings published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2003 (Volume 81, Issue 4, Page 236). 13. The World Health Organization (WHO) provided a 2004 update on the global burden of disease, published in Geneva in 2008. 14. A summary of global cholera surveillance for 2008 was published in the Weekly Epidemiological Record in 2009 (Volume 84, Issue 31, Pages 309-324). 15. Kanungo S and colleagues analyzed cholera reports in India from 1997 to 2006, with their findings published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2010 (Volume 88, Issue 3, Pages 185-191). 16. Tiruneh M studied the serodiversity and antimicrobial resistance patterns of Shigella isolates at Gondar University Teaching Hospital in Northwest Ethiopia, with findings published in the Japanese Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2009 (Volume 62, Issue 2, Pages 93-97). 17. Kerneis S and colleagues reviewed Shigella dysenteriae type 1 epidemics in refugee settings in Central Africa between 1993 and 1995, with their work published in PLoS One in 2009 (Volume 4, Issue 2, Article 4494). 18. Connolly MA and colleagues examined the impact and challenges of communicable diseases in complex emergencies, with their findings published in The Lancet in 2004 (Volume 364, Issue 9449, Pages 1974-1983). 19. Bollet AJ reviewed major infectious epidemic diseases affecting Civil War soldiers, with findings published in Infectious Diseases Clinics of North America in 2004 (Volume 18, Issue 2, Pages 293-309). 20. Chastel C commemorated the centenary of the discovery of the Vibrio El Tor strain in 1905, discussing its role in the seventh cholera pandemic, with the article published in Histoire des Sciences Médicales in 2007 (Volume 41, Issue 1, Pages 71-82).
